lc_person: Alan John Hunt (1942–2021), Carleton University sociologist and legal theorist; works include Critical Legal Studies (1987), Explorations in Law and Society (1993), and Governing Morals (1999).
item_person: Alan Hunt, the sociologist and academic linked to Alan Hunt (academic) on Wikipedia; the item retains birth year 1949 and records death in 2021.

evidence.says: LC authorizes Hunt, Alan, 1942-2021, gives fuller name Alan John, and cites Critical legal studies (1987) and Explorations in law and society (1993). A December 13, 2021 email from a Carleton University faculty member requests correction of the birth year from 1949 to 1942. The older 1949 heading remains as a variant. LC identifies VIAF 161092714 and ISNI 0000000114825976 and links Q4706911.

Q4706911 is labeled Alan Hunt, with occupations academic and sociologist and the English Wikipedia sitelink Alan Hunt (academic). It has LC n86057223, VIAF 161092714 and ISNI 0000000114825976, all matching LC. Its birth statement gives 1949, while its death statement gives 2021 and cites the Carleton memorial.

The December 16, 2021 departmental memorial states Hunt was born in 1942 and died in 2021. It identifies him as Chancellor’s Professor of Law and Sociology and lists Critical Legal Studies (1987), matching LC, alongside his work on historical sociology and moral regulation.

The institutional profile identifies Alan Hunt as Chancellor’s Professor Emeritus of Sociology and Anthropology and Law and lists Governing Morals: A Social History of Moral Regulation (1999). This matches the moral-regulation sociologist and Governing Morals attributed to alan_hunt in the local atlas evidence.

notes: The discrepancy is an outdated birth year on Wikidata, not evidence of two people: LC explicitly documents the correction to 1942, independently supported by Carleton’s memorial. The supplied key evidence is sparse, but the local alan_hunt atlas entry identifies the moral-regulation sociologist and Governing Morals (1999), matching Carleton’s profile. LC HTML was inaccessible; its public MADS/RDF record was read instead. Wikidata was read through its public entity-data endpoint.
